segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Every evening, Claire took the same train home from the city, sitting in the same seat by the window, watching the same buildings blur past.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: But tonight was different. She had stayed late at the office to finish a project, and by the time she reached the station, the platform was almost empty.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: She checked her watch and realized she had just missed the express train. The next one wasn't due for another forty minutes.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: "Great," she muttered to herself. "Just my luck." She sat down on a cold metal bench and pulled out her phone, only to find the battery had died.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: With nothing else to do, she decided to take a walk around the station to kill time.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: As she wandered past a row of vending machines, she noticed an old man sitting alone, sketching something in a worn notebook.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Curiosity got the better of her, and she walked over. "That's a beautiful drawing," she said, glancing at the sketch of the station's clock tower.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: The man looked up, surprised but pleased. "Thank you. I come here every week to draw. It helps me clear my head after a long day."

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Claire smiled. "I know the feeling. I've been staring at spreadsheets for eight hours straight."

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: They talked for a while about art, work, and the strange comfort of train stations at night. The old man, whose name was Walter, had been a schoolteacher for thirty years before retiring.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: "You know," Walter said, closing his notebook, "most people rush through life without ever stopping to notice the little things. A missed train can be a blessing in disguise."

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Claire laughed. "I guess you're right. I never would have met you otherwise."

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: As they spoke, an announcement echoed through the station: the next train was arriving in five minutes.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Walter stood up and shook her hand warmly. "It was a pleasure talking to you, Claire. Take care of yourself, and don't work too hard."

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: "You too, Walter," she replied, feeling strangely lighter than she had all day.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: When the train finally arrived, Claire took her usual seat by the window, but this time, she didn't reach for her phone. Instead, she watched the city lights fade into darkness, thinking about the unexpected conversation.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: For the first time in months, she felt like she had truly unwound, even if it was just for a few minutes in a train station.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: The next week, Claire found herself glancing at her watch again, hoping to catch the same late train. Maybe, just maybe, she thought, Walter would be there once more, sketching quietly by the vending machines.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Sometimes, she realized, the best moments in life happen when your plans fall apart.
